propositions: On the agentic execution path, accumulated tool-result message history is re-sent uncached every turn, causing input cost to grow O(N^2) in number of turns and remaining invisible to cache telemetry.

cache_settings_for sets only two of four available cache breakpoints (instructions and tool definitions) but omits the message-tail breakpoints (anthropic_cache and anthropic_cache_messages / bedrock_cache_messages) documented as necessary for multi-turn agentic workloads.

The cache-ineffectiveness warning predicate fires only when cache_read_tokens is zero, but the system block hits cache, making the counter nonzero and masking the O(N^2) growth of uncached message content.

Agentic paths require different cache-setting keys per provider: Anthropic uses anthropic_cache for automatic caching, while Bedrock uses bedrock_cache_messages, not a top-level cache_control which Bedrock rejects.
Single-turn non-agentic execution paths must remain byte-identical to avoid regression when cache settings are conditioned on execution mode.
